samples.summary: Top-level backend design doc still describes the OAuth callback contract without any `state` step, which this change makes mandatory
samples.evidence: `docs/design/backend.md:103-115` documents `GET /auth/github` as `Guard: AuthGuard('github')` (it has been `GitHubAuthGuard` and now that guard MINTS the state + sets `wafflebase_oauth_state`), and the callback as: "1. findOrCreateUser 2. createTokens 3. Sets httpOnly cookies 4. Redirects to FRONTEND_URL". After this change the callback FIRST consumes/verifies a `state` (CLI store or cookie) and 400s without one, and user creation is deliberately moved behind that check. A grep for `state` in docs/design/backend.md returns no matches at all, so the authoritative backend contract doc now describes the pre-change behaviour for a security-relevant flow. `docs/design/rest-api.md:346` and `docs/design/cli.md` WERE updated, so this is drift between sibling design docs.

samples.summary: Backend README's "Auth Flow" block describes the web login without the new state/cookie round trip
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/README.md:389-399` lists the flow as `1. Frontend links to GET /auth/github → 2. Passport redirects → 3. GitHub redirects to callback → 4. GitHubStrategy validates → 5. sign JWTs → 6. cookies → 7. redirect`. There is no step for the `wafflebase_oauth_state` cookie minted in `github-auth.guard.ts:77` nor for the callback's mandatory verification, and the endpoint table at `packages/backend/README.md:184-185` likewise still says the callback simply "sets access/refresh cookies". A reader implementing or debugging login against this README will not know a missing/mismatched `state` now yields a 400.

samples.summary: Public CLI documentation does not mention the nonce-bound callback or `--allow-unbound-callback`, so operators on an older self-hosted backend have no documented remedy
samples.evidence: `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:15-31` is the user-facing `wafflebase login` section (VitePress site, built by publish-ghpage.yml) and documents only `wafflebase login` and `--server`. A current CLI pointed at a backend that predates the nonce echo now refuses the callback and reports only `Login timed out. Try again with \`wafflebase login\`.` (deliberately, per `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:460-480`), with the escape hatch discoverable only in `packages/cli/README.md:25-30` and `--help`. `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42,121` is exactly the audience that runs a lagging backend, and it is not updated either. The schema registry entry (`packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:48`) and the package README were updated; the docs site was not.

samples.summary: api-keys commands discard the server error body that `sendJson` now supplies, unlike every other command
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:18,32,46` still do `if (!res.ok) throw httpError(res.status)`. Now that these calls route through `sendJson`/`send` (`packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:179-196`), a failed call can carry a real JSON envelope — in particular the synthesized `{ error: { code: 'SESSION_EXPIRED' } }` body from `sessionExpiredBody()` when the refresh itself was rejected. docs/notes/slides commands print that body verbatim before choosing an exit code; api-keys replaces it with the generic `Authentication failed. Run \`wafflebase login\`.`, so an agent reading stderr loses the `SESSION_EXPIRED` code the new code path just produced. Exit class is right; the body is inconsistent with the rest of the CLI.

samples.summary: `?mode=cli` with a missing/invalid port now hard-400s where it previously degraded to an ordinary web login
samples.evidence: Old guard: `if (mode === 'cli' && port) { if (valid) {...} }` — an unparsable or absent `port` fell through and the request completed as a normal browser login. New guard (`packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:85-88`) throws `BadRequestException('Invalid CLI port')` before delegating. I found no in-repo caller that relies on the old fall-through (`packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:246` always sends a valid ephemeral port, `packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:27` sends no `mode`), so the blast radius is limited to bookmarked/hand-built `/auth/github?mode=cli` URLs and third-party integrations, but the endpoint is public and the behaviour change is undocumented in `docs/design/backend.md`.

samples.summary: New test-file guard bypasses the repo's established `fixtureGitEnv` helper, leaving the fixtures themselves unscoped
samples.evidence: The diff protects `scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs` with a module-scope `for (const name of Object.keys(process.env)) if (name.startsWith('GIT_')) delete process.env[name]`. Every other git-fixture suite in this repo instead passes `env: fixtureGitEnv(dir)` per call — `scripts/agent/novelty.test.mjs:245`, `scripts/agent/eval/run.test.mjs:133,635`, `scripts/agent/collect-captures.test.mjs:1298` — and `scripts/agent/git-env.mjs:112-127` documents that as the required form for WRITE paths precisely because it also pins `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` so no discovery happens. The fixtures here (`scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:80,417,482,533,640,704,728`) still spawn `git init`/`git commit` with `cwd` only and now rely on a process-global mutation performed after ESM import evaluation. It works today, but it diverges from the convention the rest of the harness enforces, so a future test in this file that restores the environment (or a helper imported later that snapshots it) silently reintroduces the repository-corruption bug this change exists to fix.

searchedFor: grep changed-areas across repo (verify-self.mjs, ci.yml, harness.config.json)
finding.summary: The GIT_* scrubbing added by this change lives only in the test file; the production module it protects still spawns git with an inherited environment
finding.evidence: scripts/test/changed-areas.test.mjs:50 deletes every `GIT_*` var from `process.env` at module scope, and its comment explains the hazard: git exports `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` to hooks, and `verify:self` runs from `pre-push`. But the module under test is unchanged: `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:255` (`resolveRefs`'s `git()` helper) and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:350` (`git diff --name-only ${base}...${head}`) call `execFileSync("git", …, { cwd: repoRoot })` with **no `env`**, so under a hook they answer about whatever `GIT_DIR` names, not `repoRoot`. `scripts/verify-self.mjs:8` imports those very functions and is the pre-push entry point (it is careful enough to read HEAD via `readHeadSha`, see verify-self.mjs:543-547). The repo already ships the canonical fix — `repoScopedEnv()` / `fixtureGitEnv()` in scripts/agent/git-env.mjs:102,120 — and neither changed-areas.mjs nor the new test uses it. Impact: a hook-run lane selection computed against the wrong repository, i.e. CI lanes silently skipped. Fix belongs on scripts/changed-areas.mjs (pass `repoScopedEnv(repoRoot)`), not on the test.

verdict.reason: The finding claims scripts/changed-areas.mjs spawns git with an inherited environment and never uses repoScopedEnv. Both claims are false in this working tree. changed-areas.mjs:36 imports repoScopedEnv from ./agent/git-env.mjs. The two exact call sites named by the finding both pass it: resolveRefs's git() helper at changed-areas.mjs:257-267 uses `env: repoScopedEnv(repoRoot)` (with an inline comment at 259-263 describing the precise GIT_DIR/pre-push hazard the reviewer raises), and changedPaths's `git diff --name-only ${base}...${head}` at changed-areas.mjs:358-364 uses `env: repoScopedEnv(repoRoot)` with the comment "Scoped for the same reason as resolveRefs's reads above." repoScopedEnv (agent/git-env.mjs:102-110, via stripped() at 75-82) deletes every GIT_LOCATION_VARS entry including GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE, and sets GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to repoRoot's parent to cap discovery. So under a pre-push hook the diff is computed against repoRoot, and the claimed impact (lane selection against the wrong repository) cannot occur on these paths. The reviewer's cited line numbers (255, 350) are off by roughly the inserted env lines and comments versus the real 257/358, consistent with reading a pre-change version of the file. The production guard the finding says is missing is present at both sites.
